sub: Pay less for data you rarely use.

Overview.p: Storage classes balance price and access speed: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant, Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Glacier Deep Archive.
A fridge for daily food, a store room for rare items, a locked cellar for old things.
A hospital keeps recent scans in Standard and moves old ones to Deep Archive.

items: Or move objects with lifecycle rules
A colder class means cheaper storage
Retrieval time and fees go up

items: Change its class to Standard-IA in Properties
Upload another file as Glacier Instant Retrieval
Compare prices on the S3 pricing page
Create a lifecycle rule to move files after 30 days

code: aws s3 cp data.zip s3://company-demo-123/ --storage-class STANDARD_IA

Practical.p: Terminate or delete everything you created after practice to avoid charges.

Examples.p: Standard 30 days, then IA, then Glacier.

code: aws s3 cp f.zip s3://company-demo-123/ --storage-class GLACIER_IR
aws s3api restore-object --bucket company-demo-123 --key old.zip --restore-request Days=7

CLI Commands.p: IDs like i-0abc123 and sg-0abc123 are examples. Replace them with your real IDs.

items: 30 days for Standard-IA and One Zone-IA.
Flexible Retrieval takes minutes to hours. Deep Archive takes hours (about 12 for standard retrieval).
